title: Generators
description:
A coroutine can hand out a value with `co_yield`, pause exactly where it is, and carry on from that point when it is asked for the next one. `std::generator<T>` (C++23) is the ready-made return type for that.

Write two generators:

- `std::generator<int> countdown(int from)`: yields `from`, `from - 1`, ... down to `1`.
- `std::generator<long long> fibonacci()`: yields 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5 ... **for ever**. An endless loop is fine in a generator: it only runs as far as the caller asks.

A generator is a range, so the caller can loop over it or cut it short with `std::views::take`.
hints: `countdown` is a loop with `co_yield i;` inside; when it ends, the generator is finished.
`fibonacci` keeps `a` and `b`, and loops for ever: `co_yield a;` then moves on with `auto next{ a + b }; a = b; b = next;`.
